result:
I reviewed the actual diff (not the self-report), then verified independently: ran `tsc --noEmit` (clean), `eslint` on all 11 changed/added files (clean), and the new test files plus the pre-existing voice-ticket-service test (all pass, 7/7 new + no regressions). Confirmed the tier1 classification is correct — no `.github/workflows/**` or tier2-triggering paths (migrations/schema/auth/permission/payment/billing/rls/security) touched.

**Verdict: approve (tier1).**

Architecture is sound: shared `createDocumentRecord()` extraction reuses the existing storage/document pattern, tenant scoping goes through `withTenantContext` everywhere and is backed by a real (non-mocked-self-certifying) isolation test, and the auth/actor patterns match ~30 other existing v1/projexa routes rather than inventing something new.

Two minor, non-blocking issues logged for follow-up in `review-verdict.json`: (1) `externalUrl` on documents/drawings isn't scheme-validated, a theoretical stored-XSS vector if the frontend ever renders it as a raw link; (2) caller-supplied `metadata` on the generic documents POST can set `isExternalLink: true` on a real upload, causing a cosmetically broken link later (not a data leak, since the bucket is private).
